_review_status: DRAFT general guidance. Must be reviewed and edited by an agricultural extension officer (AGRITEX) before farmers use it.

healthy.summary: This leaf shows no sign of maize leaf blight or maize streak virus, the two diseases this tool looks for.
steps: Keep checking your crop every week, especially after rain and during warm, humid spells.
Photograph the leaf again if you notice streaks, long tan spots or leaf damage.
Remember that this tool does not check for pests such as fall armyworm or for nutrient problems.
healthy.get_help: Contact your extension officer if the plants look unhealthy even though this leaf looks fine.

maize_leaf_blight.summary: Long, grey-green to tan spots shaped like cigars on the leaves point to maize leaf blight (northern corn leaf blight). It spreads fastest in cool, wet, humid weather.
steps: Walk through the field and note how many plants have the long tan spots, and whether they are on the upper leaves.
Avoid working among the plants while the leaves are wet, so you do not carry the spores.
After harvest, bury or plough in infected crop residue and rotate with a crop that is not a cereal.
Next season, ask your seed supplier or extension officer for blight-tolerant varieties.
Ask your extension officer before buying or spraying any fungicide. It is only worthwhile in some situations.
maize_leaf_blight.get_help: Contact your extension officer soon if many plants are affected before tasselling.

maize_streak_virus.summary: Thin yellow streaks running along the leaf veins point to maize streak virus. Small insects called leafhoppers carry it from plant to plant. Infected plants cannot be cured.
steps: Pull out badly affected young plants early and bury or burn them so they stop feeding the leafhoppers.
Weed the field and its edges, because wild grasses carry both the virus and the insects.
Avoid planting next to older maize or very late plantings, which keep leafhoppers around.
Next season, ask your seed supplier or extension officer for streak-tolerant varieties.
Do not spray fungicide. This is a virus, so fungicide will not help.
maize_streak_virus.get_help: Contact your extension officer if the streaks are spreading across the field.

uncertain.summary: The tool could not tell clearly what this photo shows, so please do not rely on the result.
steps: Take a new photo of a single leaf that fills most of the picture.
Use daylight, avoid strong shadows and direct sun, and hold the phone steady so the leaf is sharp.
Photograph a leaf that shows the problem, and include the whole width of the leaf.
uncertain.get_help: If the new photo is still unclear, show the plant to your extension officer.
